register.access_notes: Fetched over HTTPS with the standard WebFetch client, requests spaced roughly 2 seconds apart; 8 requests in total (the KRS title/chapter index three times for verbatim chapter titles, footer links and the Chapter 304 subtitle list, plus chapter pages for 337, 278, 383, 61 and 304.12). All returned 200. IMPORTANT: two hosts serve this register. apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/ serves the statute text and worked every time. The SharePoint host legislature.ky.gov returned HTTP 403 Forbidden for the policy pages (https://legislature.ky.gov/policies-security/Pages/Disclaimers.aspx and https://legislature.ky.gov/Pages/disclaimer.aspx), so the formal disclaimer/terms page could not be read; I stopped rather than retrying or changing client identity. licence.summary: The register asserts blanket copyright in its footer ('Copyright Kentucky Legislative Research Commission / All rights Reserved') and the statute pages add that catchlines and headings are not part of the law. The formal Disclaimers page is 403 to scripted access, so the full terms could not be read. Under the government edicts doctrine (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)) the text of the Kentucky Revised Statutes as enacted is not copyrightable and is freely reusable and adaptable; what the LRC can plausibly claim is its editorial apparatus (chapter titles, centred headings, section catchlines, explanatory and annotation notes), which the site itself says 'do not constitute any part of the law'. Marked not-open because the register makes an unqualified all-rights-reserved assertion that a human should resolve before relying on it.

acts.title: Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 337 - Wages and Hours
acts.verified_how: Fetched the KRS chapter index at apps.legislature.ky.gov/law/statutes/, which prints the entry '337 WAGES AND HOURS', and then the chapter page itself (chapter.aspx?id=38890): live sections include .020 Time of payment of wages, .055 Payment of all wages upon dismissal or leaving, .060 Unlawful withholding of wages, .070 Employer wage deduction statements, .275 Minimum wage, .285 Overtime compensation, .385 Employer liability for unpaid wages, with the 1974/1978-repealed sections shown as repealed. Page states 'Includes enactments through the 2026 Regular Session' and 'The KRS database was last updated on 09/22/2026'.
acts.notes: Minimum wage, overtime, wage statements, deductions and the wage-claim remedy are all in this chapter.

acts.title: Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 337 - Wages and Hours
acts.verified_how: Same chapter page fetch (chapter.aspx?id=38890) as at 09/22/2026: '.015 Leave of absence for employee to receive adoptive child', '.100 Volunteer firefighter/emergency worker absences', '.355 Lunch period requirements', '.365 Employee rest periods', '.415 Court-ordered appearance protection' all shown as live.
acts.notes: Kentucky has no general statutory entitlement to paid vacation, paid holidays or paid sick leave; the only statutory leave is adoption leave (KRS 337.015) plus protected absences for volunteer emergency responders and court attendance, and mandated meal/rest breaks. KRS Chapter 304 Subtitle 53 'Paid Family Leave Insurance Act' (verified as an index entry) regulates a voluntary insurance product offered by insurers - it does not create an employee leave entitlement. Family and medical leave for eligible employees is federal (29 U.S.C. 2601, FMLA).

acts.title: Kentucky Revised Statutes Chapter 337 - Wages and Hours
acts.verified_how: Same chapter page fetch (chapter.aspx?id=38890) as at 09/22/2026: section '.055 Payment of all wages upon dismissal or leaving' shown as live.
acts.notes: Kentucky is an at-will state with no statutory severance entitlement and no state mini-WARN Act; the only statutory termination duty is timely payment of all wages due on dismissal or resignation (KRS 337.055). Mass-layoff and plant-closing notice is federal (29 U.S.C. 2101, WARN). Unemployment compensation on job loss is KRS Chapter 341.

licence.summary: The Office of the Revisor of Statutes asserts no copyright anywhere on the statutes pages - there is no copyright line in the footer and no terms-of-use or permissions page; the only notices are a currency statement, a warning that the text may change without notice, and a disclaimer that the office cannot give legal advice. Combined with the government edicts doctrine (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)), under which the text of the Maine Revised Statutes as enacted is not copyrightable, both reuse and adaptation are permitted. Maine's official consolidation is produced in-house by the Revisor's Office and served free on the Legislature's own site, so there is no commercial-publisher layer over the statute text (the annotated print edition, Maine Revised Statutes Annotated, is a Thomson Reuters product and its annotations are separately copyrighted - use the Revisor's site, not the annotated edition).

topic_gaps.reason: No Maryland statute. Air passenger rights are federal (49 U.S.C. 41712; 14 C.F.R. Part 250 oversold flights, Part 259 tarmac delays) and state regulation of air carrier prices, routes and services is pre-empted by 49 U.S.C. 41713; intercity rail is Amtrak under 49 U.S.C. Subtitle V Part C. Maryland's MARC and MTA services set passenger rights by tariff and regulation, not by statutory compensation entitlement.

Federal matter. US states are constitutionally barred from laying imposts or duties on imports or exports (U.S. Const. art. I, s.10, cl.2); customs law is 19 U.S.C. and the Harmonized Tariff Schedule.

Federal matter. Immigration and employment authorisation are governed by the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.), including employment verification at 8 U.S.C. 1324a; states have no power to issue work permits.

licence.summary: NOT VERIFIED. The register's own pages, including any terms or copyright notice, could not be reached (see access_notes), so nothing is asserted here from first-hand reading. What can be said without reading the site: under the government edicts doctrine (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)) the text of the General Laws as enacted is not copyrightable and is freely reusable and adaptable. Two Massachusetts-specific wrinkles a human should check on the register itself: (a) a web search indicates malegislature.gov carries a notice that its version of the General Laws is NOT the official version - the official text is the biennially published edition, with the session laws (Acts and Resolves of Massachusetts) compiled and published by the Secretary of the Commonwealth - so the authoritative citation may need to be the printed edition; and (b) the annotated commercial editions (Massachusetts General Laws Annotated, Thomson Reuters; and the LexisNexis Annotated Laws of Massachusetts) carry separately copyrighted annotations. Both points come from search results, not from the register, and are flagged rather than relied on. open_licence is left false because the condition for setting it true - having read the register's terms and found reuse and adaptation permitted - was not met.
